tldr: Chatwoot now checks the health of each WhatsApp Cloud number every 6 hours and stores the result on the channel. The Account Health page shows more details and guides admins on authorization errors.
goal: Let admins see a WhatsApp number at risk, such as a low quality rating or a restriction, before customers stop getting replies.

story.heading: An hourly job now schedules health syncs
story.body: Every hour, the scheduler queues 1 sync per WhatsApp Cloud channel not checked in 6 hours, at most 25 per run.

story.heading: Health is now stored on the WhatsApp channel
story.body: 3 new columns hold the last health, its check time and the last error. The scheduler orders the channels by the check time.

story.heading: HealthService reads 2 Graph API resources
story.body: It reads the phone number and its business account, and uses Graph API version 24 or later for the health fields.

story.heading: Only the newest check is written
story.body: update_all writes the result only when no later check exists. A risky quality rating or status goes to the log once per change.

story.heading: Account Health page shows the new details
story.body: It shows the phone, capacity, business account, webhook and recovery details. An authorization error leads the admin to the Configuration flow.

story.heading: The whole change
story.body: Background jobs call the WhatsApp adapter, which stores the health on the channel. The inbox health endpoint now syncs and stores it too.

components.summary: Account Health shows phone, capacity, business account and webhook details, and guides admins on authorization errors.
The hourly job now queues HealthSyncSchedulerJob, which queues HealthSyncJob per channel.
HealthService syncs and stores the number's health for the jobs and the health endpoint, raises ApiError and logs risky changes.
New phone_number_health columns and an index on the WhatsApp channel table.

decisions.title: Store the health on the channel
decisions.why: The scheduler picks channels by the last check time. The error column keeps the reason of the last failed check for the admins.
decisions.alternative: Keep the health only in memory, for the current request.

decisions.title: A scheduler job and 1 job per channel
decisions.why: The scheduler picks the channels with the oldest check, at most 25 per hour. A failing number does not stop the others.
decisions.alternative: A single job that checks every channel in a loop.

decisions.title: Write with update_all, not save
decisions.why: Health polling must skip credential validation, timestamps, inbox touches and audit callbacks of the channel.

decisions.title: Write only when no newer check exists
decisions.why: The where clause on phone_number_health_checked_at keeps an older, slower check from replacing a newer result.
decisions.alternative: Always write the last result that arrives.

decisions.title: A typed ApiError with Meta's code
decisions.why: Code 190 marks an authorization error. The page then guides the admin to reconnect, without Meta's technical codes.
decisions.alternative: Raise a string error with the response body.
